resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. slides §1 (referent resolution) line 62: scope: I verified the facts. The judge's reading of check_slides.md §1 doesn't make this a blocking failure.

What checks out:
- Line 62 is "Ask the agent to explain both using your own rows."
- The chunk titled "Phase 3: Scorer runs the benchmark" lists three metrics at lines 56-58: precision, recall and coverage.
- "both" implies two, so there is a count mismatch.
- The line arrived in commit 1b176d30 (2026-11-01). The slides PASS at 4d9c4af2 (2026-08-25) predates it, so the pin does not cover this line.

Why it fails as a blocking §1 finding:
1. §1's test is "THIS chunk plus earlier chunks of the same file", and the Phase 3 `##` chunk runs from line 50 to line 65. The sentence at line 62 is a lead-in to the very next element in that chunk, prompt 6 at line 64. Prompt 6 is a paste block reading "Tell me about precision and recall." The reader sees that pair on the same slide, one line below the pointer, so "both" resolves at once.
2. Prompt 5, also on this slide, says "Compute precision (...) and recall (...)" and then treats coverage separately as "Coverage = how many of the 30 claims the detector looked at". That marks precision and recall as the pair. It marks coverage as a count, not a quality metric you would ask the agent to explain.
3. §1 says fenced blocks are exempt from being flagged. It does not say they stop being context. A chunk's fenced prompt is on the slide, so it counts as part of the chunk the test is applied to.
4. §1's "Never named" subtype is aimed at referents that appear nowhere in the file, or only on a LATER slide. Here the referent sits on the same slide, so the failure the rule targets does not apply.
5. §1's "Vague with full history" subtype requires a pronoun that "stays ambiguous even holding every prior slide". This one is disambiguated by the slide's own paste block, so it does not stay ambiguous.

Residual issue: the sentence is slightly imprecise, since "both" sits under a three-item list. That is a nit-level wording polish, not a BLOCK. The finding should be downgraded or dropped, not applied as blocking.
